## Conventions used by every card (R2.4 to R2.9)

**What a card is.** A card fixes the files, the interfaces, the test cases (name, arrange, act, assert) and
the commands of one task. The writing-plans skill expands it to bite-sized steps with the line-by-line code at
the start of its release, which is why every card ends with `Expand to steps at release start: yes`. A card is
not a placeholder: every open point in it carries a `(DP-…)` or `(pending D-n)` marker.

**Why the cards name symbols as well as paths.** They were written against the working tree at `HEAD`
`3bc7f6ca` (the CRM paths are identical on `main@caa7f112`) and each path, line, name, route, permission,
event and table was re-read on 2026-10-07. Earlier releases (R1.x, R2.1 to R2.3) will change files that later
cards touch, so a card names what it **Consumes** from them by symbol and the expansion re-reads those symbols
first. Lines in `libs/platform-core/src/platform_core/auth.py` move when `fix/ci-failures` merges, so cards cite
that file by symbol.

**Markers.**
- `path:line` is verified by reading the file at `HEAD`. A path with no marker exists at `HEAD`.
- `Create` carries the verified parent directory. A new directory under a verified parent says so.
- `(inference)` is a conclusion not observed in code or on the box.
- `(DP-<release>-<n>)` is a plan decision the spec leaves open or words inconsistently. The release's
  self-review checklist lists each one so the reviewer can confirm it before the expansion.
- `(pending D-n)` is an owner decision still open: the card builds the registry's recommended default.
- **Recording an owner's answer (R1.1's contract for `docs/adr/0038-crm-programme-decisions.md`).** The ADR's Decisions table has one row per decision (`| D-n |`, six cells, the last the State: `open (default recommended)`, `approved YYYY-MM-DD` or `amended YYYY-MM-DD`). **The owner sets the State cell; an agent never does.** A gate reads it with `grep -E '^\| D-n \|.*\| (approved|amended) [0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2} \|$' docs/adr/0038-crm-programme-decisions.md`, which prints the row once answered and nothing while open (for D-9, which needs `approved` alone, the pattern drops `amended`: spec §2.1). **Evidence that travels with an answer** (D-9's signed security review, D-21's staff plan action, D-3's count, D-10's census) goes on one line under `## Sign-offs`, `D-n: <what was signed or done> on <date>`; a Sign-offs line is evidence and never an answer. When the owner answers D-n, the same commit replaces the `(pending D-n)` clause in each note that cites it (`grep -rn 'pending D-n' docs` lists them). The spec words the same facts as "D-n: <answer> on <date>" lines; **R1.1's table is what exists, so the cards follow it** (DP-2.4-6).
- **OWNER RUN** is an act only the owner takes: a production read or write, a box `.env` edit, a deploy, a
  fleet tool, a reconcile, an SPA publish. An agent builds and tests it and never runs it (P§3 F11,
  ADR-0036 decision 1). No card step touches the box, a production database or the network.
- Register "rows" in `docs/adr/open-questions-register.md` are cited by file line (`:97`, `:98`, `:122`,
  `:135`), because the spec's "row 97" means line 97 of that 154-line file (only its first table has ids,
  and `:56` is id 20).

**Standard checks.** Every command runs from the repository root. Database tests need the local stack
(`make infra`, then `make migrate`). `import app` is ambiguous across services, so a service is always
tested and typechecked from its own directory.

| Check | Command |
|---|---|
| Service tests | `cd services/<svc> && uv run pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider` (one file: replace `tests` with the path) |
| Service types | `cd services/<svc> && uv run mypy app` |
| Layering | `cd services/<svc> && PYTHONPATH=. uv run lint-imports --config ../../.importlinter --no-cache` |
| Lint, format, hygiene | `uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .` then `make hygiene` |
| Libs and contracts | `uv run pytest libs -q` and `uv run pytest libs/contracts -q` (`make contracts-check`) |
| Repository tooling | `uv run pytest tests/infra -q` (`make test-infra`: no database, no broker) |
| OpenAPI and permission manifest | `make openapi`, then `make openapi-check` |
| One service's migrations | `cd services/<svc> && ../../tools/roundtrip.sh` and `cd services/<svc> && uv run alembic check`; all services: `make migration-roundtrip` then `make migration-check` |
| Frontend (CRM app) | `cd frontend && pnpm --filter @opsgrids/product-crm typecheck`, `... lint`, `... test`, `... build`; one file: `cd frontend/product-crm && pnpm vitest run <path>`; whole row: `make frontend-gate`; visual: `make ui-visual`; accept a reviewed baseline: `cd frontend && pnpm visual:update` |
| Everything | `make gate` (Actions billing is blocked, so local gate output is the evidence the owner merges on) |

**Test conventions** (the repo's own). Database tests carry `pytestmark = pytest.mark.integration`, use the
service's real-Postgres fixtures on the NOBYPASSRLS app role (`session`, `client`, `org_id`, `data`,
`admin_session` for seeding another tenant's rows), and read back through `session.expire_all()` after a handler
wrote through another connection. Every internal route gets three negative tests (no token 401, wrong caller
403, wrong organization claim 403) in the shape of `services/deal/tests/test_lead_conversion_internal.py:52-56,123-140`.
Every public route gets 401, 403 (missing permission), 403 (scope below the floor) where a floor exists, 402
(no `crm` entitlement) and a cross-tenant case. Every consumer gets a redelivery test. Every migration gets an
upgrade, a downgrade, RLS-forced and grant checks, and a round trip.

**Git.** One branch per release (`feat/crm-r2-<n>-<slug>`, from `main`), one PR per release, squash-merged by
the owner. Commit messages are `Area: what changed`, as in `git log` ("Purge tool: process a sub-organisation
before its parent"), and never mention an AI, an assistant or a tool that generated anything; no trailers.
Never commit `.env` or a secret.

## Release R2.4 - Aborted-conversion consumers, log-only first

Spec §7 (registry NEW-9: A22, C55, EV43, EV44, F1 to F3, F5, F7, F8, H3, I8, W13). `crm.lead.conversion_aborted`
gets its first consumers. **Deal** soft-deletes the aborted attempt's orphan deal; **customer** soft-deletes the
orphan contact and company; each only when it can prove the record is the attempt's own and untouched since.
Nothing acts on first deploy: both services start with `CRM_CONVERSION_CLEANUP_MODE=log_only` and write nothing
until the owner flips the flag. The release also folds deal's first consumer into its API process (+1 MB, which
is why the owner raises `EDGE_BUDGET_ACCEPTED_MB` first), adds deal's references probe route, and keeps compose,
the memory budget, the ops-monitor queue list and the RUNBOOK literals in lockstep. No migration, no schema, no
OpenAPI change (internal routers are outside the OpenAPI document).

### Prerequisites

- **Releases.** R2.1 merged **and deployed** (DD-23): its event carries the pre-bump `generation` and the
  `claim_id`, and R2.4's handlers ignore an event without them. R1.1 merged (it creates `docs/crm.md` and
  `docs/adr/0038-crm-programme-decisions.md`, which Task 2.4.11 edits). R1.2a and R1.2b are not required.
- **Why R2.4 follows R2.1 although the registry's rule is "a new consumer deploys before its producer's behaviour
  changes" (registry §D).** An event staged before a queue is bound is dropped while its outbox row is marked
  published (`libs/platform-core/src/platform_core/events.py:250-262`, `:465-471`), so nothing a log-only handler
  would have done is lost by that order; consumers ignore an event with no `generation`; and nothing destructive
  can run before the owner sets `on`, which happens only after both releases are deployed and the soak has been
  read. The consumers (in `log_only`) are what deploys first; the **arming** is the separate, later owner act.
- **Decisions** (the card that depends on an open row does not start before the owner answers it, P§11):
  D-1 (orphan deal: soft-delete with an audit row naming the consumer, no `stage_changed`), D-2 (customer cleanup
  only of provable records, never a reused one, **log-only first**), D-3 (a sweep is built only if the owner's
  read-only count is non-zero), and D-13 as amended by registry L17 (every consumer fold is +1 MB; the owner
  raises the ceiling by one). The cards build the recommended defaults.
- **OWNER RUN items (spec §13).** O-4 the D-3 count, O-5 the ceiling edit, O-6 the deploy and its reads, O-7 the
  soak and the flip. Nothing in the cards runs any of them.
- **Branch.** `feat/crm-r2-4-conversion-cleanup`, cut from `main` after R2.1 is on `main`.

### Deploy order and verification

All commands run from the owner's checkout of the merged `main` (the Makefile is read there) against the box.
`HOST=deploy@<ip>` and `CONFIRM=edge.opsgrids.com` are the owner's values.

1. **Agent, before the PR is opened.** `make gate` locally; paste the output into the PR. The rows that matter:
   `typecheck` (every service imports `platform_core`), `test-infra`, `test-libs`, `test-services`,
   `contracts-check`, `openapi-check` (unchanged), `migration-roundtrip` and `migration-check` (unchanged: no
   revision is added). Also run, by hand, the opt-in sweep database test if Task 2.4.10 was built.
2. **OWNER RUN, before anything else: the D-3 count (read-only).** On the box, from `infrastructure/edge/`:

   ```bash
   docker compose -f compose.prod.yml --env-file .env exec -T postgres psql -U opsgrids -d opsgrids -At -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 \
     -c "SET default_transaction_read_only = on" \
     -c "SELECT a.organization_id,
                count(*) FILTER (WHERE a.action = 'lead.conversion_aborted' AND a.after ? 'conversion_generation') AS owner_changed_aborts,
                count(*) FILTER (WHERE a.action = 'lead.conversion_aborted' AND NOT (a.after ? 'conversion_generation')) AS status_changed_aborts,
                count(*) FILTER (WHERE a.action = 'lead.conversion_failed'  AND a.after ? 'conversion_generation') AS deleted_record_bumps
           FROM lead.audit_logs a
          WHERE a.action IN ('lead.conversion_aborted', 'lead.conversion_failed')
          GROUP BY a.organization_id ORDER BY a.organization_id"
   ```

   Record the three counts per organization in `docs/crm.md` and in `docs/adr/open-questions-register.md:122`
   (Task 2.4.11). If `owner_changed_aborts + deleted_record_bumps` is zero for every organization, Task 2.4.10 is
   **not built**.
3. **OWNER RUN: answer D-1, D-2, D-3 and the memory ceiling (D-13), review, squash-merge.**
4. **OWNER RUN: raise the ceiling before the deploy.** Edit the box's `.env` (mode 600; an agent never edits it):
   `EDGE_BUDGET_ACCEPTED_MB=3945`. Then `make edge-preflight HOST=… CONFIRM=…` (read-only) must print a
   post-deploy total of 3945 MB and accept the ceiling. Without this step the deploy's own preflight refuses
   before anything changes (K-2): a delay, not a hazard.
5. **OWNER RUN: deploy in a quiet window.** `make deploy HOST=… CONFIRM=… REF=<sha>`. The diff touches
   `libs/platform-core/src/platform_core/ops_monitor/config.py`, so `needs_full_rebuild` is true
   (`infrastructure/edge/lib/rebuild-decision.sh:37-38`): **every image rebuilds and recreates** (the script's own
   comment records a 502 for an invitation accepted mid-deploy, `:18-24`). No migration runs for any service.
6. **OWNER RUN: verify, read-only.**

   ```bash
   make edge-status HOST=… CONFIRM=…
   make edge-logs   HOST=… CONFIRM=… SERVICE=deal     TAIL=400 | grep -E 'consumer.started|crm.conversion_cleanup'
   make edge-logs   HOST=… CONFIRM=… SERVICE=customer TAIL=400 | grep -E 'consumer.started|crm.conversion_cleanup'
   ```

   Expect `deal` healthy with a zero restart count; `consumer.started` with `queue=deal.events` and
   `bindings=['crm.lead.conversion_aborted']` in deal's log, and the second binding beside
   `crm.pipeline.activity.logged` in customer's. On the box:
   `docker compose -f compose.prod.yml --env-file .env exec -T rabbitmq rabbitmqctl list_bindings source_name destination_name routing_key | grep conversion_aborted`
   lists both queues (`rabbitmq` is the compose service named in `RABBITMQ_URL`, `compose.prod.yml:57-105`: inference).
   The `ops-monitor /status` block that `make edge-status` prints must carry an observation `dlq.deal.events`
   (`libs/platform-core/src/platform_core/ops_monitor/checks.py:189-212`: detail `deal.events.dlq: N message(s) parked`,
   or `not declared yet` until the consumer has run once). `docker stats --no-stream` for the `deal` container reads about 1 MB above its previous idle figure (the
   priced measurement is arm64 and the box is amd64: read the **delta**, not the absolute).
7. **OWNER RUN: soak in `log_only`.** Read `crm.conversion_cleanup.would_apply` and `would_keep` lines (ids and
   counts only) with the two `make edge-logs` commands above and check any against the lead's audit rows. Aborts
   are rare by construction (`CONVERSION_LEASE_SECONDS = 60`, `services/lead/app/domain.py:93`; upstream timeouts of
   5 s), so the soak may see none; the owner decides how long to wait and what absence of evidence is worth.
8. **OWNER RUN: flip, only after reading the soak (pending D-2).** Edit the box's `.env`:
   `CRM_CONVERSION_CLEANUP_MODE=on`; then `docker compose -f compose.prod.yml --env-file .env up -d customer deal`
   (the pattern of `infrastructure/edge/RUNBOOK.md:1162`). Both services flip together (DD-21): never one without the
   other. The start-up log line states the effective mode.
9. **Memory** after the deploy (`python3 infrastructure/edge/lib/memory_budget_totals.py infrastructure/edge/memory-budget.json --profiles …`):
   core 1772 MB, `crm` 2068 MB, the ten sellable profiles 3748 MB (97.0%), the ten plus `admin` 3945 MB (102.1%);
   `deal` is `api_with_worker` (99), `deal-worker` is `background` under `split-workers` (priced 0 while the profile
   is off). Up to two more Postgres connections per deal process, opened lazily (`max_connections=400`,
   `compose.prod.yml:263`).

### Rollback

In order of preference, each independent of the others (spec §7.9):

1. **Stop acting without a deploy (OWNER RUN).** Set `CRM_CONVERSION_CLEANUP_MODE=log_only` (or `off`) in the box
   `.env` and recreate `customer` and `deal` with the command of step 8. Takes effect for the next message.
2. **Undo what was done (OWNER RUN, owner SQL).** Every deletion is soft and carries an audit row with
   `acting_as = 'crm-conversion-cleanup'` and the lead and generation in `reason`; restoring is clearing
   `deleted_at` on the rows those audit rows name. No code does it. The `deleted` events already published are not
   recalled; no subscribable key reacts to them.
3. **Code rollback (OWNER RUN).** `make edge-rollback HOST=… CONFIRM=…` redeploys the previous ref (a full rebuild
   again). `deal.events` and its binding stay on the broker as an inert queue (near-zero volume); nothing was
   migrated, so nothing is skipped.
4. **Un-fold without un-shipping** (`RUN_CONSUMERS_IN_API=false` plus `split-workers` in `EDGE_PROFILES`) starts
   `deal-worker`, a background container priced at 90 MB that the box's ceiling probably cannot absorb. Prefer 1.

**Stop conditions.** Any `consumer.handler.dead_lettered` line in `deal` or `customer`, or depth on
`deal.events.dlq` or `customer.events.dlq`; any `crm.conversion_cleanup.applied` for records the owner did not
expect; a rise in `409 company-deleted` on `leads/{id}:convert` after the flip; either container restarting.
Attribute a dead letter with the `queue=` field of the `consumer.handler.dead_lettered` line: every `.dlq` is
bound `#` to the one shared dead-letter exchange and no `x-dead-letter-routing-key` is set
(`libs/platform-core/src/platform_core/events.py:461-469`), so a dead letter from any consumer can appear in every
`.dlq` and a non-zero depth on `deal.events.dlq` is not by itself proof that deal's handler failed (inference from
RabbitMQ semantics, not verified without a broker).

**Steps**

2. Generate the vector file once from lead's real function (a throwaway, not committed; never regenerate it, the

   ```bash
   mkdir -p libs/contracts/vectors
   cd services/lead && uv run python - <<'PY' > ../../libs/contracts/vectors/conversion_ids.v1.json
   import json, uuid
   from app.domain import _CONVERSION_NAMESPACE, conversion_ids

   vectors = []
   for n in range(1, 7):
       lead_id = uuid.UUID(f"6c1d0000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000{n}")
       for generation in (0, 1, 2, 7):
           company, contact, deal = conversion_ids(lead_id, generation)

                     "templates": {"company": "{lead_id}:company{suffix}", "contact": "{lead_id}:contact{suffix}",
                                   "deal": "{lead_id}:deal{suffix}"},
                     "suffix": {"generation_0": "", "generation_n": ":{generation}"}, "vectors": vectors}, indent=2))
   PY
   ```

Commit: `git add libs/contracts/vectors libs/contracts/tests/test_conversion_id_vectors.py services/deal/app/domain.py services/customer/app/domain.py services/lead/tests/test_domain.py services/deal/tests/test_conversion_cleanup_ids.py services/customer/tests/test_conversion_cleanup_ids.py && git commit -m "CRM: pin lead conversion ids with golden vectors and add the deal and customer copies"`.

**Files**

**Interfaces**

  Query: `company_id: uuid.UUID` (required), `contact_id: uuid.UUID | None`, `exclude_deal_id: uuid.UUID | None`.
  Response `ReferencesOut {company_deal_count: int, contact_deal_count: int, company_activity_count: int, contact_activity_count: int}`,
  four non-negative integers, **counts only, no ids**.
  Auth: `require_service_token` (router dependency), `_require_caller(request, "customer")`, `_require_org_claim`, tenant bound from the path inside `async with session.begin():`

  Deals counted: live (`deleted_at IS NULL`) with `company_id = :company_id`, and for the contact `primary_contact_id = :contact_id`.
  `exclude_deal_id` is removed from the two deal counts **only when that deal is disposable**: absent, soft-deleted, or live and `is_pristine_lead_deal` (DD-20; registry `C55` carries the same disposable-only rule, folded from the spec's first-draft tightening of its earlier "unconditionally").

### Task 2.4.8: Customer's three-phase handler for `crm.lead.conversion_aborted`

**Files**
- Modify: `services/customer/app/consumers.py` (add `customer_conversion_aborted` and its binding beside `crm.pipeline.activity.logged`, `:97`)
- Modify: `services/customer/app/services.py` (add `plan_conversion_cleanup` and `apply_conversion_cleanup`, or keep them private in `consumers.py` if they stay under about 120 lines: the expansion decides)
- Modify: `services/customer/tests/helpers.py` (add `CONTRACTS_ROOT` and `aborted_envelope`, as Task 2.4.5)
- Create: `services/customer/tests/test_conversion_cleanup.py`

**Interfaces**
- Consumes: Tasks 2.4.1 (`conversion_ids`), 2.4.2 (mode), 2.4.6 (locked selectors, `acting_as`/`reason` deletes, audit rows), 2.4.7 (`deal_references`); `service_ctx` (`services.py:141`).
- Produces: `@dataclass(frozen=True) class CleanupOutcome: mode: str; ignored: str | None; contact: str | None; company: str | None` with the codes `deleted`, `would_delete`, `would_keep`,
  `absent`, `already_deleted`, `not_derived_id`, `not_created_by_attempt`, `touched`, `adopted`, `other_contacts`, `referenced`;
  `async def run_conversion_cleanup(envelope) -> CleanupOutcome` and the registered `async def customer_conversion_aborted(envelope) -> None`; `consumer.on("crm.lead.conversion_aborted")(customer_conversion_aborted)` on `customer.events`.
- Parsing, before any phase (added at assembly: the card named these rules for deal only, and customer's handler deletes a contact and a company): the event is parsed by customer's own copy of the rules Task 2.4.5 lists for deal (`import app` is ambiguous across services, so there is no shared parser), and is ignored, with a log line and an acknowledgement, when `generation` is absent or not an integer of at least 0 (`type(generation) is int`: a JSON boolean is rejected), `claim_id` is absent, a uuid does not parse, the envelope's top-level `organization_id` disagrees with the payload's, `reason` is not one of `status_changed`, `owner_changed`, `record_deleted`, or the mode is `off`. An ignored event reads no row, calls no probe and writes no ledger row; `CleanupOutcome.ignored` is `mode_off`, `no_generation`, `bad_generation`, `no_claim_id`, `bad_uuid`, `org_mismatch` or `unknown_reason`.
- Phases (DD-19; `tests/infra/test_io_outside_transaction.py` forbids a network call inside `session_scope(` / `.begin(` / `_work_scope(`):
  1. **Plan**: a read-only transaction (`SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY` first); `already_processed`; the derived company and contact in any state; every provenance rule that needs no other service (below). It ends before anything else happens.
  2. **Probe** (no transaction open): only if the plan contemplates deleting the company or the contact, `deal_references(settings, org, company_id=<derived>, contact_id=<derived or None>, exclude_deal_id=<derived deal id>)`.
     Any `ReferencesProbeUnavailable` **raises**, which earns the one redelivery and then the DLQ (`events.py:496-516`); acknowledging would lose the cleanup silently. In `log_only` the probe still runs (a "would apply" is only honest with deal's answer), so an unreachable deal in `log_only` also redelivers and the dead letter is the signal the owner should see before flipping.
  3. **Act** (`on` only): a new transaction; `already_processed` again; `FOR UPDATE` the company and contact; re-verify every rule under the locks (a rep or a later attempt may have changed them since phase 1); if the plan still holds, soft-delete the **contact then the company**
     with `acting_as="crm-conversion-cleanup"` and `reason="lead_conversion_aborted:<lead_id>:g<generation>"` (`delete_company` refuses while a live contact exists, `services.py:573-577`); `mark_processed` in **every** `on` outcome, a decision to keep included.
- Provenance (spec §7.4): the contact is deletable only if its id is the derived contact id, it is live, its audit history is exactly one row (`contact.created`, `acting_as='lead'`) and `last_activity_at IS NULL`;
  the company only if its id is the derived company id, it is live, its audit history is exactly one row (`company.created`, `acting_as='lead'`), **no live contact other than the derived contact names it**, and the probe answers zero deals and zero activities for the company and for the derived contact.
  **(DP-2.4-4)** Two implications the spec's table leaves implicit. (a) The probe carries the contact's own two counts for the same reason DD-20 gives for the company (a deal that deal keeps still points at the contact through `primary_contact_id`), so the contact is deleted only when `contact_deal_count` and `contact_activity_count` are zero as well.
  (b) A company whose derived contact is live and **kept** is kept with code `other_contacts`, because `delete_company` would refuse (inference from `services.py:573-577`). Confirm both when D-2 is answered.
  A lead with no email has no derived contact (the payload's `contact_id` is null) and only the company is considered.

**Test cases** (`test_conversion_cleanup.py`; the autouse engine fixture; a monkeypatched `consumers.deal_references` fake)
- Ignore rules (added at assembly): `test_customer_ignores_every_event_the_deal_handler_ignores` — parametrised over the seven rules above (no `generation`; `"1"`, `1.5`, `-1`, `True` and `None` as the generation; no `claim_id`; a malformed uuid; an envelope whose organization disagrees with its payload; an unknown reason; mode `off`); arrange: `aborted_envelope(...)` mutated to break one rule, a pristine derived company and contact seeded in **both** organizations, a probe fake that fails the test if it is called; act: `run_conversion_cleanup`; assert no exception, `outcome.ignored` is the named code, the probe was never called, every seeded row is still live, and there is no audit row beyond the creations, no outbox row and no ledger row.
- Phases: `test_the_probe_runs_with_no_transaction_open` — arrange: wrap `consumers._session_scope` in a counter of open scopes and a fake probe that asserts the count is 0; act: an `on` event; assert the probe was called once;
  `test_a_probe_failure_raises_so_the_message_is_redelivered` — parametrise the fake over `ReferencesProbeUnavailable` for a timeout, a connection error, a 500 and a 403; assert the handler raises and no ledger row exists;
  `test_log_only_runs_the_probe_and_writes_nothing` — assert the probe was called, outcome `would_delete`, no audit/outbox/ledger rows; `test_off_does_not_call_the_probe`; `test_nothing_to_delete_never_calls_the_probe` (both records kept or absent: assert zero probe calls);
  `test_the_act_phase_reverifies_under_locks` — arrange: the company is edited between the phases (the fake probe edits it); assert it is kept; `test_the_probe_receives_the_derived_ids_and_the_derived_deal_as_the_exclusion` (added).
- Provenance:
  `test_a_company_and_contact_created_by_the_attempt_are_soft_deleted_contact_first` — assert `acting_as`/`reason` on both audit rows and the outbox order `crm.book.contact.deleted` then `crm.book.company.deleted`;
  `test_a_company_reused_by_name_is_kept` (two audit rows: `adopted`); `test_a_contact_reused_by_email_is_kept` (parametrise the three reuse shapes: no phone, gap-fill, differing phone);
  `test_a_company_edited_after_creation_is_kept`; `test_a_contact_with_activity_is_kept` (`last_activity_at` set: `touched`); `test_a_company_with_another_live_contact_is_kept` (`other_contacts`);

### Task 2.4.10: The historical sweep tool (CONDITIONAL: built only if the owner's D-3 count is non-zero)

Build this card **only** if the count of Release R2.4's deploy-order step 2 shows `owner_changed_aborts + deleted_record_bumps` greater than zero for some organization. A pre-R2.1 `status_changed` abort recorded no generation and did not bump, so the records it left sit at the generation the lead still derives from and a re-qualified lead adopts them by id: they are not orphans and **no code deletes them** (spec §7.4). If the count is zero, this card is skipped, the file does not exist, and Task 2.4.11 records the zeros (AC-2.4-14).

**Files**
- Create: `tools/sweep_aborted_conversions.py` (parent `tools` verified; `make typecheck-tools` runs `uv run mypy tools`)
- Create: `tests/infra/test_sweep_aborted_conversions.py` (static; runs in the gate)
- Create: `tests/infra/test_sweep_aborted_conversions_db.py` (opt-in)

**Interfaces**
- Consumes: both services' `run_conversion_cleanup(envelope) -> CleanupOutcome` (Tasks 2.4.5, 2.4.8: **the tool decides nothing about safety; the handlers do**, DD-48), `lead.audit_logs` and `lead.leads` (read only), `conversion_ids`.
- Produces `tools/sweep_aborted_conversions.py {report|apply}`; default `report`. Flags `--org <uuid>` or `--all`, `--pace MS` (default 250); `apply` is a dry run unless `--apply`, `--confirm-count N` (the count the dry run printed), `--i-took-a-backup` **and** `--i-know-this-is-the-live-database` are all given
  (the gating of `tools/purge_test_orgs.py:1893-1910`). One child process per service, `--child --service lead|customer|deal`, because `import app` is ambiguous: the `lead` child reads candidates and writes an ids-only `candidates.json`; the `customer` and `deal` children replay them.
  Sweepable rows only: a `lead.conversion_aborted` audit row whose `after` has `conversion_generation` (an owner-changed abort; aborted generation = recorded - 1) and a `lead.conversion_failed` row that has it (a deleted-record bump). Each becomes a synthetic envelope: `event_type` `crm.lead.conversion_aborted`,
  `event_id = uuid5(SWEEP_NAMESPACE, f"{organization_id}:{lead_id}:{generation}")` (a re-run is idempotent through each service's ledger), a payload valid against R2.1's schema, `claim_id` a deterministic synthetic uuid.
  `report` is read-only (`SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY` in every child; handlers in `log_only`): it **re-reads the lead's current state** (`converted_company_id`, `converted_contact_id`, `converted_deal_id`, `conversion_generation`) and drops any candidate whose derived ids equal the lead's converted ids or whose generation is not strictly below the lead's current one, then prints counts per organization and per decision code, ids only.
  `apply`: one transaction per organization per service on the NOBYPASSRLS app role with the tenant GUC bound, stop at the first failing organization, pace between organizations, output counts and ids only, one audit row per organization per service naming the tool (`acting_as="sweep-aborted-conversions-cli"`).
- **(DP-2.4-5) Invocation.** This is a destruction tool, so ADR-0036 decision 1 applies in full: no `make` target and no `remote.sh` subcommand. The RUNBOOK (Task 2.4.11) gives the owner the exact throwaway-container lines, the shape `reconcile_permissions` uses
  (`infrastructure/edge/remote.sh:450-457`): `docker compose -f compose.prod.yml --env-file .env run --rm --no-deps -T -e PYTHONPATH=/app -v "$(pwd)/../../tools:/opt/tools:ro" <service> python /opt/tools/sweep_aborted_conversions.py --child --service <service> ...`.

**Test cases**
- Static (`test_sweep_aborted_conversions.py`): `test_each_gate_flag_is_refused_without_its_partner` (parametrise the three), `test_the_dry_run_is_the_default`, `test_confirm_count_must_equal_the_dry_run_count`, `test_the_output_contains_ids_and_counts_only` (a world full of emails and names: no `@` and no name in stdout or stderr), `test_the_synthetic_envelope_validates_against_the_committed_schema`, `test_a_status_changed_abort_row_is_never_sweepable`.
- Opt-in database (`test_sweep_aborted_conversions_db.py`, `pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not REAL_DSN, reason="set OPSGRIDS_SWEEP_TEST_DATABASE_URL to a migrated throwaway database (as opsgrids_admin)")`, which `make hygiene` accepts because it names a reason):
  `test_report_equals_the_apply_set`, `test_a_lead_converted_since_is_never_swept`, `test_a_rerun_is_a_no_op`, `test_a_touched_orphan_is_kept`. The gate skips the file; **it is a manual step of this release's verification**: `make migrate` into a throwaway database, then
  `OPSGRIDS_SWEEP_TEST_DATABASE_URL=... uv run pytest tests/infra/test_sweep_aborted_conversions_db.py`, and paste the pass count into the pull request. The decision logic itself is proved by the handler tests, which run in `make test-services`.

**Steps**
1. Write the static tests; run red: `uv run pytest tests/infra/test_sweep_aborted_conversions.py -q`.
2. Implement the parent (argument parsing, gating, child sequencing) and the three children on the `tools/reconcile_membership_links.py` pattern (`_DryRunRollback`, `ACTING_AS`, paced loop, `:100-120`).
3. Write and run the opt-in database test by hand as above; run `uv run mypy tools` and `make hygiene`.
4. Commit: `git add tools/sweep_aborted_conversions.py tests/infra/test_sweep_aborted_conversions.py tests/infra/test_sweep_aborted_conversions_db.py && git commit -m "Tools: add the owner-run sweep for orphans an aborted conversion left before the consumers existed"`.

## Release R2.5 - Stage authoring API and `crm.pipeline.stage.write`

Spec §8 (registry C2 to C5, E18, EV14, EV8 `reason`, EV46's notification skip, H6's `ORG=`, G26's SPA hardening). An ORG-scope admin can add, rename, reorder and archive pipeline stages through four routes, behind one new
permission whose route floor is ORG (pending D-6), with every invariant the stage tables cannot hold by themselves enforced under one exclusive lock. It is the first release in which an organization can leave the virtual default, so it also carries
the notification rule that stops an archive-driven mass move from firing tenant automations, **and the one SPA change that lets the published bundle survive a stage it has never heard of** (DD-54), and an `ORG=` option on the reconcile
so the new code reaches one designated tenant before the fleet. No migration (the tables are R2.3's), no stage-editing screen (SP3's R3.4).

### Prerequisites

- **Releases.** R2.3 merged **and deployed and verified on its own** (spec §6.8). R2.5 consumes, by name, what R2.3 produces: tables `deal.pipelines` and `deal.pipeline_stages` (composite organization-scoped foreign key, the identity trigger that freezes `key`, `pipeline_id`, `organization_id`, `outcome`, RLS forced);
  the pure module `services/deal/app/pipeline.py` (`StageSpec`, `PipelineSpec`, `DEFAULT_PIPELINE`, `validate`, `PipelineInvalid`); `selectors.load_pipeline_spec`; `services.lock_pipeline_shared`, `services.lock_pipeline_exclusive`, `services.materialise_default_pipeline`; `GET /deals/stages`; the `DealOut` fields `stage_label`, `stage_outcome`, `stage_position`, `stage_is_last_open`, `closed_at`.
  None of these exists at `HEAD` (`services/deal/app` has no `pipeline.py` today), so each card re-reads the real symbol at expansion. R1.1 merged (docs).
- **Decisions.** D-6 (default: `crm.pipeline.stage.write`, route floor ORG, read stays under `crm.pipeline.deal.read`, no new admin template). The cards build the default.
- **OWNER RUN items.** O-8 in order: publish the hardened SPA first, deploy, reconcile one designated tenant (dry run, then apply), smoke it including the Deals screen, then reconcile the fleet (dry run, then apply).
- **Why "the filter before the route" is met by the reconcile and not by the order of two image recreations (DD-50).** Until the reconcile no existing user holds the code, so the four routes answer 403 to everyone; a brand-new activation that reaches the new code through the manifest's bind mount has no tenant automations to fire and, with the SPA already hardened, no screen to break.
- **Branch.** `feat/crm-r2-5-stage-authoring`.

### Deploy order and verification

1. **Agent.** `make gate` locally, output pasted into the PR. Rows that matter: `typecheck`, `test-infra` (the new reconcile-wrapper test), `test-services` (deal and notification), `contracts-check`, `openapi-check` (regenerated `deal.json` and `crm.json`), `frontend-gate`, and `make ui-visual` with the reviewed baseline change. CODEOWNERS applies to `libs/contracts/`.
2. **OWNER RUN: review and squash-merge.**
3. **OWNER RUN: publish the hardened SPA first (DD-54).** Check out the merged `main` first (the bundle is built from the local checkout, not from the deployed ref), then:

   ```bash
   make edge-web HOST=… CONFIRM=… APP=crm
   ```

   Prove the right tree was built: the published bundle contains the board column's accessible name. On the box, from `infrastructure/edge/`:
   `grep -rl "Other stages" "$(sed -n 's/^EDGE_WEB_ROOT=//p' .env | head -1)/crm/current"` must list at least one file (the bundle is published under `$EDGE_WEB_ROOT/<app>/{releases,current}`, `infrastructure/edge/publish-web.sh:26-28`, host `revenue.opsgrids.com`, `:105-110`).
   It is safe before anything else: it reads fields R2.3's deal image already emits and, where they are absent, derives them from the legacy six.
4. **OWNER RUN: deploy.** `make deploy HOST=… CONFIRM=… REF=<sha>`. `libs/contracts` is excluded from the full-rebuild rule (`rebuild-decision.sh:38`), `remote.sh` and the Makefile are not images, so **`deal` and `notification` rebuild and nothing else**. No migration. (`remote.sh` on the box is brought up to date by this deploy, which is what step 5's `--org` needs.)
5. **OWNER RUN: verify, read-only.** `make edge-status HOST=… CONFIRM=…`; `make edge-logs HOST=… CONFIRM=… SERVICE=deal TAIL=200` and `SERVICE=notification TAIL=200` are clean.
6. **OWNER RUN: reconcile one designated tenant (registry E.4 step 4).** `ORG=` is forwarded by the Makefile in the owner's checkout of the merged `main` (the one used for step 3):

   ```bash
   make edge-reconcile HOST=… CONFIRM=… PRODUCTS=crm ORG=<designated tenant uuid>            # prints that tenant's dry run only
   make edge-reconcile HOST=… CONFIRM=… PRODUCTS=crm ORG=<designated tenant uuid> APPLY=1    # after reading it
   ```

   Expect `grants_added` of one code on `CRM_PIPELINE_ADMIN`, a `pv` bump, no `roles_created`. Among existing tenants only that one now holds the code.
7. **OWNER RUN: smoke on that tenant (a write).** Sign in as that tenant's administrator; `GET /api/v1/deals/stages` (virtual, `materialised: false`); `POST /api/v1/deals/stages` with a label (the first write materialises the default pipeline); `PATCH` it; `POST /api/v1/deals/stages:reorder`; `POST /api/v1/deals/stages/{id}:archive` it.
   Read the trail, on the box from `infrastructure/edge/`:

   ```bash
   docker compose -f compose.prod.yml --env-file .env exec -T postgres psql -U opsgrids -d opsgrids -At -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 \
     -c "SET default_transaction_read_only = on" \
     -c "SELECT action, count(*) FROM deal.audit_logs WHERE organization_id = '<designated tenant uuid>' AND action LIKE 'pipeline.%' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1" \
     -c "SELECT event_type, count(*) FROM deal.outbox WHERE organization_id = '<designated tenant uuid>' AND event_type LIKE 'crm.pipeline.stage.%' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1"
   ```

   Use a tenant that has a `stage_changed` rule or automation and archive a stage that moves a test deal: **confirm no WhatsApp or email fired for the moved deal.** Then, **as a user of that tenant, open the Deals screen** (board, list, a deal's detail, the CSV export) with a deal in the custom stage: it renders by its label and nothing throws.
8. **OWNER RUN: reconcile the fleet, only after step 7 passed**, off-peak and paced (250 ms; the reconcile bumps `pv` and members refresh tokens lazily, `tools/reconcile_permissions.py:75-82`):

   ```bash
   make edge-reconcile HOST=… CONFIRM=… PRODUCTS=crm            # dry run: the designated tenant shows an empty diff; every other organization shows grants_added of one code on CRM_PIPELINE_ADMIN and a pv bump, no roles_created
   make edge-reconcile HOST=… CONFIRM=… PRODUCTS=crm APPLY=1
   ```
9. **Memory.** No container changes; the totals are R2.4's (core 1772, `crm` 2068, ten profiles 3748, ten plus `admin` 3945).

### Rollback

`make edge-rollback HOST=… CONFIRM=…` redeploys the previous ref; the deal image reverts to R2.3's, which still *reads* the tables, so organizations that customised their stages keep working and simply cannot edit them. The permission stays in the manifest and in reconciled roles (the platform has no way to remove a code; an inert code is harmless).
**Do not roll back below R2.3 while any organization has a custom stage or a deal in one**: R2.3's downgrade guard refuses it for exactly that reason. **The SPA is the same one-way door:** `make edge-web-rollback HOST=… CONFIRM=… APP=crm` (the `APP=crm` is required: the target defaults to the storefront's `buyer` bundle, `Makefile:625`) restores a bundle that cannot render a stage outside the legacy six,
so **do not roll the SPA back below this release's bundle while any organization holds one.** The owner's read-only check, in the `psql` pattern above: `SELECT organization_id, count(*) FROM deal.pipeline_stages WHERE key NOT IN ('lead','qualified','proposal','negotiation','closed_won','closed_lost') GROUP BY 1`, and the same filter on `deal.deals.stage`.
**Stop conditions:** any 5xx on the four routes; a `pipeline_busy` that persists after the transaction that caused it has ended; a tenant automation firing for an archive-driven move; a deal whose `stage` is an archived `open` stage; a Deals screen that fails to render for a tenant holding a custom stage (a defect in the hardening: fix forward and **pause the fleet reconcile** until it is fixed).

### Task 2.5.2: The stage-authoring rules as pure functions

**Files**
- Modify: `services/deal/app/pipeline.py` (created by R2.3; the pure module, no I/O)
- Create: `services/deal/tests/test_pipeline_authoring_domain.py` (pure, no database)

**Interfaces**
- Consumes (R2.3): `StageSpec(key, label, position, outcome, default_probability, tone, archived=False, id=None)`, `PipelineSpec(stages, id, key, name, materialised)` with `.get`, `.active`, `.entry_stage`, `.outcome_of`, `.is_last_open`, `validate(stages) -> None` raising `PipelineInvalid(code)`.
- Produces (names are the plan's, DD-24, DD-45, DD-41):
  - `raw_slug(label: str) -> str`: NFKD-normalise, drop non-ASCII, lower-case, collapse every run outside `[a-z0-9]` to `_`, trim `_`, cut to 20 characters; empty when the label holds no ASCII letter or digit. `slugify_label(label: str) -> str` is `raw_slug(label) or "stage"`: `stage` when nothing is left.
  - `generate_key(label: str, taken: Collection[str]) -> str`: `taken` is every key of the pipeline **including archived stages** plus the six legacy keys; on collision append `_2`, `_3`, `_4` in turn, cutting the base so the whole key stays within 20 characters. A key is never reused.
  - `normalise_label(raw: str) -> str`: trim, collapse internal whitespace to single spaces; raises `PipelineInvalid("label_invalid")` when empty, over 80 characters or holding a control character.
  - `label_collides_with_key(label: str, other_keys: Collection[str]) -> bool`: the label lower-cased, or its `raw_slug` when that is not empty, equals a **different** stage's key (a stage's own key is allowed). **(DP-2.5-4)** A label with no ASCII letter or digit (a stage named in Devanagari, Gujarati or Tamil, which this product's tenants may well use) has an empty raw slug and collides with nothing. DD-45 says "slugified"; read with `slugify_label`'s `stage` fallback, it would refuse the second such label as colliding with the first one's fallback key `stage`. `generate_key` still gives each such label a key: `stage`, then `stage_2`, `stage_3`.
  - `propose_create(spec, *, label, outcome, default_probability, tone, after_stage_id) -> tuple[StageSpec, ...]`, `propose_update(spec, stage_id, *, label=None, tone=None, default_probability=None) -> tuple[StageSpec, ...]`, `propose_reorder(spec, stage_ids) -> tuple[StageSpec, ...]`,
    `propose_archive(spec, stage_id, *, move_open_deals_to, deals_in_stage) -> ArchivePlan` where `ArchivePlan(stages: tuple[StageSpec, ...], move_target: StageSpec | None)`. Each returns the **proposed full stage set** with dense positions among active stages, already run through `validate`, or raises `PipelineInvalid(code)`.
  - `PipelineInvalid.code` values used here: `label_invalid`, `duplicate_label`, `label_collides_with_key`, `probability_pinned`, `probability_required`, `after_stage_invalid`, `stage_set_mismatch`, `closed_stage_before_open`, `stage_archived`, `last_stage_of_outcome`, `move_target_required`, `invalid_move_target`, `move_target_not_allowed`, `stage_not_found`. (Task 2.5.4 maps them to 404, 409 and 422.)
- Placement (spec §8.4.3): without `after_stage_id` an `open` stage goes after the last open stage and a closed stage at the very end; with it the stage goes immediately after that active stage, and a placement that would put a closed stage before an open one is `after_stage_invalid`. `won` forces 100 and `lost` 0 (a supplied different figure is `probability_pinned`); `open` requires a probability. An omitted tone is `info` for open, `success` for won, `danger` for lost.

**Test cases** (pure; arrange a `PipelineSpec`, act one function, assert the returned set or the `PipelineInvalid.code`)
- Keys: `test_slugify_normalises_accents_case_and_runs`, `test_slugify_cuts_to_20_and_falls_back_to_stage`, `test_generate_key_suffixes_on_collision_with_an_archived_key`, `test_generate_key_never_returns_a_legacy_key` (label "Lead" yields `lead_2`), `test_generate_key_cuts_the_base_so_the_suffixed_key_fits_20`; `test_labels_with_no_ascii_letters_get_the_fallback_key_then_numbered_ones` (added at assembly) — arrange: the labels "प्रस्ताव", "વાટાઘાટ" and "முன்மொழிவு" and a `taken` set holding the six legacy keys; act: `generate_key` for each in turn, adding each result to `taken`; assert `stage`, `stage_2`, `stage_3`.
- Labels: `test_normalise_label_trims_and_collapses`, `test_normalise_label_refuses_empty_overlong_and_control_characters`, `test_a_label_equal_to_another_stages_key_collides_lower_cased_and_slugified` (including "Closed Lost" vs `closed_lost`), `test_a_label_equal_to_its_own_key_does_not_collide`, `test_duplicate_active_label_is_refused_case_insensitively`, `test_an_archived_label_can_be_reused`; `test_a_label_in_another_script_never_collides_with_a_fallback_key` (added at assembly) — arrange: a pipeline whose active stage "प्रस्ताव" holds the key `stage`; act: `label_collides_with_key("વાટાઘાટ", {"stage"})` and `propose_create` with that label; assert `False` and a proposed stage with key `stage_2` and the label unchanged, while `label_collides_with_key("Stage", {"stage"})` is still `True`.

### Task 2.5.3: The authoring services: lock, materialise, validate, write, audit, events, archive moves

**Files**
- Modify: `services/deal/app/services.py` (add `create_stage`, `update_stage`, `reorder_stages`, `archive_stage`; give `lock_pipeline_shared` its timeout; add event constants beside `EVT_DEAL_*`, `:43-47`)
- Modify: `services/deal/app/selectors.py` (add `get_stage`, `count_deals_in_stage`, `live_deals_in_stage_batch`)
- Create: `services/deal/tests/test_stage_services.py`

**Interfaces**
- Consumes: Task 2.5.2's `propose_*`; R2.3's `lock_pipeline_exclusive`, `lock_pipeline_shared`, `materialise_default_pipeline`, `load_pipeline_spec`; `record_audit` and `publish_event`; `move_stage`'s semantics (`services.py:296-347`).
- Produces:
  - `async def create_stage(session, ctx, *, label, outcome, default_probability, tone, after_stage_id, request=None) -> StageSpec`; `async def update_stage(session, ctx, stage_id, *, changes: dict[str, Any], request=None) -> StageSpec`; `async def reorder_stages(session, ctx, stage_ids, *, request=None) -> PipelineSpec`; `async def archive_stage(session, ctx, stage_id, *, move_open_deals_to, request=None) -> tuple[StageSpec, int]` (the stage and the number of deals moved).
  - Every one begins with `_begin_stage_write(session, ctx) -> PipelineSpec`: (1) `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'` and `SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '30s'`, (2) the **exclusive pipeline lock as the first statement of the write**, (3) `materialise_default_pipeline` if the organization has none (once, under that lock), (4) load the spec, build the proposed set, `validate`, and only then write. A refusal writes nothing, the materialisation included (the request's transaction rolls back).
  - `lock_pipeline_shared(session, org)` now runs `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'` immediately before its lock request and `RESET lock_timeout` right after the lock is granted, so only the pipeline-lock wait can time out. A lock timeout (SQLSTATE 55P03) becomes `PipelineBusyProblem(ConflictProblem)`, `errors=[{"code": "pipeline_busy", ...}]`, `headers={"Retry-After": "2"}` (`ProblemError` carries `errors` and `headers`, `libs/platform-core/src/platform_core/errors.py:24-54`). No function takes the shared and then the exclusive lock (a lock upgrade can deadlock).
  - Audit actions: `pipeline.stage_created`, `pipeline.stage_updated` (before and after of the changed fields), `pipeline.stage_reordered`, `pipeline.stage_archived`; per moved deal `deal.stage_changed` with `acting_as = "pipeline-stage-archive"` and `reason = "stage_archived"`. **(DP-2.5-1)** The spec fixes the action names and leaves the audit `entity` and the event `aggregate_type` open: the plan uses `entity = "pipeline_stage"` and `aggregate_type = "pipeline_stage"` for create, update and archive, and `"pipeline"` for reorder.
  - `PIPELINE_LOCK_TIMEOUT: Final = "5s"` (a module constant the concurrency tests monkeypatch to `"300ms"`, so no test waits five seconds).
  - Events (Task 2.5.5): `crm.pipeline.stage.created|updated|archived|reordered`; per moved deal `crm.pipeline.deal.stage_changed` with `reason = "stage_archived"`.
  - Archive of an `open` stage that holds **any** deal, live or soft-deleted, needs `move_open_deals_to` (an active `open` stage other than itself): the **live** deals move in batches of 200 rows per statement inside the same transaction, **each keeping its own probability** (DD-25), each with its own audit row and event; more than 2,000 live deals is `too_many_deals` and nothing moves; soft-deleted deals stay put; a deal never moves into a closed outcome by an archive.
    Archive of a `won` or `lost` stage is allowed only while another active stage of the same outcome remains; no deal is touched; a target is refused. Archiving an archived stage returns the stage and writes nothing. There is no un-archive and no delete (a static test bans deleting a stage).
    **(DP-2.5-3)** Whether the moves are one set-based statement per batch plus per-deal audit and outbox inserts, or a loop over `move_stage` taking `reason` and `acting_as`, is the expansion's choice; the tests pin the outputs.

**Test cases** (`test_stage_services.py`, service level, real database)
- `test_the_exclusive_lock_is_the_first_statement_of_a_stage_write` — arrange: a `before_cursor_execute` listener recording statements; act: `create_stage`; assert the advisory-lock statement precedes every other statement after the two `SET LOCAL`s.
- `test_the_two_timeouts_are_transaction_local` — assert `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'` and `SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '30s'` were executed and neither value survives the transaction.
- `test_lock_pipeline_shared_sets_and_resets_its_lock_timeout` — assert the `SET LOCAL` precedes the lock and `RESET lock_timeout` follows it.
- `test_a_refused_write_changes_nothing` — act: a duplicate label; assert the pipeline and stage row counts, audit rows and outbox rows are unchanged, the materialisation included.
- `test_the_first_write_materialises_the_default_exactly_once_and_writes_one_materialised_audit_row` — assert six rows plus the new one and one `pipeline.materialised` row (R2.3, DD-26).
- `test_archive_batches_of_200_keep_each_deals_probability_and_write_one_audit_row_and_one_event_each` — arrange: 450 live deals at distinct probabilities; assert 450 moved, probabilities unchanged, 450 `deal.stage_changed` rows with `reason = 'stage_archived'`, 450 outbox events carrying `reason`.
- `test_archive_over_2000_live_deals_moves_nothing` — arrange 2,001 live deals; assert `too_many_deals` and no row changed.
- `test_a_soft_deleted_deal_in_the_stage_still_requires_a_target_but_is_not_moved` — arrange: only soft-deleted deals remain; assert `move_target_required` without a target and, with one, the soft-deleted deal stays in the archived stage.
- `test_archiving_an_archived_stage_writes_nothing` — second call returns the stage; audit and outbox row counts unchanged.
- `test_no_code_path_deletes_a_stage` (static) — an AST scan of `services/deal/app` finds no `delete(PipelineStage)` and no `DELETE FROM` against the stage table.

**Steps**

2. Implement `_begin_stage_write` and the four services on Task 2.5.2's `propose_*`; add the selectors; add `PipelineBusyProblem`; update `lock_pipeline_shared`. Every query filters on `organization_id` in addition to the forced RLS policy.
3. Green; `cd services/deal && uv run mypy app`; layering; `uv run pytest tests/infra/test_io_outside_transaction.py -q`.
4. Commit: `git add services/deal/app/services.py services/deal/app/selectors.py services/deal/tests/test_stage_services.py && git commit -m "Deal: add the stage-authoring services behind the exclusive pipeline lock"`.

- Error mapping (RFC 7807 through `platform_core.errors`; `errors[]` entries `{field, code, message}`): 401/403/402 as everywhere; 404 `not-found` `stage_not_found` (unknown, other-organization or deleted stage id: RLS plus the organization filter);

  422 `validation`: `label_invalid`, `label_collides_with_key`, `probability_pinned`, `probability_required`, `after_stage_invalid`, `stage_set_mismatch`, `closed_stage_before_open`, `move_target_required`, `invalid_move_target`, `move_target_not_allowed`. A single function `problem_for(exc: PipelineInvalid) -> ProblemError` owns the mapping.
- Idempotence: `PATCH`, `:reorder` and `:archive` are idempotent by construction; `POST /deals/stages` is not, but a repeated submission meets `duplicate_label`, which a client treats as already created. No idempotency-key header is introduced.

**Test cases** (`test_stage_routes.py`; `as_principal(principal_for(...))` as in `services/deal/tests/test_authz.py:27-32`; parametrised over the routes unless named)
- Negative authz: `test_no_token_is_401`; `test_a_principal_without_stage_write_is_403` (arrange: holds `crm.pipeline.deal.write:ORG`; assert 403 on all four); `test_stage_write_at_own_scope_is_403_below_the_floor` (arrange: `crm.pipeline.stage.write:OWN`; assert 403 `requires ORG scope`);

  `test_a_write_in_organization_a_never_changes_organization_b` (arrange: B has a materialised pipeline; assert B's stage and audit rows are identical before and after A's four writes).
- Behaviour: `test_create_generates_the_key_server_side_and_refuses_a_client_key`, `test_create_places_open_and_closed_stages_correctly`, `test_create_refuses_a_closed_stage_before_an_open_one`, `test_won_and_lost_pin_their_probability_and_a_wrong_figure_is_422`,

### Task 2.5.8: `ORG=` on the permission reconcile

**Files**
- Modify: `infrastructure/edge/remote.sh` (`reconcile_permissions` `:434-448`, `_reconcile_run` `:450-457`, the dispatch line `:552`)
- Modify: `Makefile` (`edge-reconcile`, `:584-587`)
- Create: `tests/infra/test_remote_reconcile_org.py`
- Modify: `infrastructure/edge/RUNBOOK.md` (the command table row at `:56`; Task 2.5.10)

**Interfaces**
- Produces: `remote.sh reconcile-permissions <product[,product…]> [--apply] [--org <uuid>]`. Today the dispatch passes exactly two arguments (`reconcile_permissions "${2:-}" "${3:-}"`) and `_reconcile_run` hard-wires `--all` (`:456`) although `tools/reconcile_permissions.py` already takes `--org <uuid>` (`:59`, `:328`) and the two are mutually exclusive.
  The function takes the products first, then any of `--apply` and `--org <uuid>` in any order; a missing value after `--org`, or a value that is not a uuid (`^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-([0-9a-fA-F]{4}-){3}[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$`), is refused with exit 64 **before any container starts**; with a valid `--org` the tool is run with `--org <uuid>` and **not** `--all`, for every product of the list; without `--org` the call is exactly today's (`--all`, `--dry-run` first, then `--apply`).
  The dispatch becomes `reconcile-permissions) shift; reconcile_permissions "$@" ;;`.
- Make: `edge-reconcile` accepts `ORG=<uuid>` and forwards `--org $(ORG)`; **(DP-2.5-2)** the target also refuses a non-uuid `ORG` before any `ssh`, because Make interpolates the value unquoted into a command that `ssh` hands to the box's shell (inference: the value would otherwise be interpreted there). Both checks use the same pattern; the box's check is the authoritative one.

**Test cases** (`tests/infra/test_remote_reconcile_org.py`, static: the real functions sliced out of `remote.sh` as `tests/infra/test_remote_state_dir.py:75-80` does for `ensure_ops_monitor_state_dir`, run in a throwaway shell with a fake `docker` first on `PATH` that records its arguments; the harness defines `COMPOSE=(docker compose)` and a `log` function, and runs from `infrastructure/edge/` so `../..` resolves)
- `test_org_passes_org_and_not_all` — act: `reconcile_permissions crm --org <uuid>`; assert every recorded `docker` line ends with `reconcile_permissions.py crm --org <uuid> --dry-run` or `... --org <uuid>` and none contains `--all`.
- `test_without_org_the_call_is_exactly_todays` — act: `crm --apply` and `crm`; assert the recorded lines are `crm --all --dry-run` then `crm --all` for apply, and `crm --all --dry-run` only for the dry run, byte for byte what the recorded lines were before this change.
- `test_a_non_uuid_org_is_refused_before_any_container_runs` — parametrise `not-a-uuid`, `$(id)`, `1234`, `` (empty); assert exit 64 and an empty docker log.
- `test_org_without_a_value_is_refused` (added) — `crm --org` with no value; exit 64, empty log.
- `test_org_is_passed_to_every_product_of_a_list` — act: `crm,finance --org <uuid>`; assert both products' lines carry `--org <uuid>`.
- `test_apply_and_org_in_either_order_behave_the_same` (added) — act: `crm --apply --org U` and `crm --org U --apply`; assert identical recorded lines.
- `test_the_make_target_forwards_org` — act: `make -n edge-reconcile HOST=h CONFIRM=c PRODUCTS=crm ORG=<uuid> APPLY=1`; assert the printed ssh line ends `reconcile-permissions crm --apply --org <uuid>`.
- `test_the_make_target_refuses_a_non_uuid_org_before_ssh` (added, DP-2.5-2) — act: `make edge-reconcile HOST=h CONFIRM=c PRODUCTS=crm ORG='x; rm -rf /'`; assert a non-zero exit and that no `ssh` line was printed or run.

**Steps**
1. Write the test file; run red: `uv run pytest tests/infra/test_remote_reconcile_org.py -q`.
2. Rewrite the two shell functions and the dispatch line; keep tabs for indentation as the rest of the file does; add the `Makefile` validation and forwarding.
3. Green; `make shellcheck` (pinned shellcheck over every script, `Makefile:484`); `uv run pytest tests/infra -q`.
4. Commit: `git add infrastructure/edge/remote.sh Makefile tests/infra/test_remote_reconcile_org.py && git commit -m "Edge: let the permission reconcile target one organization"`.

## Release R2.6 - C15 expand: the roster knows memberships, and the mapping tool exists

Spec §9 (registry B1 to B3, C25 to C27, C57, C49 as dual resolution only, F4, H1 built and tested, W17, G16's owner-display half, B2's `revert` evidence, C26's error codes). R2.6 prepares C15 **without changing who can see or edit anything**: `customer.owners.membership_id`; an append-only, reversible mapping journal in each of customer, deal and lead;
account's bulk membership read; team activation (a roster row created *from a member*) and a candidates list; dual resolution at every roster lookup, so a reference is a membership id **or** the legacy roster id; `tools/map_crm_owners.py` built, tested and wired for the owner to run (**`apply` is not run in this release**); and an SPA that resolves and offers both kinds of id,
so a rewritten row never renders as a blank owner whenever the owner chooses to run the data step. `ScopeContext`, every OWN comparison and every default owner stay on the employee link until R2.7.

### Prerequisites

- **Releases.** R2.2 deployed (the release train's need: R2.7 consumes `OwnerSubject`; R2.6 itself leaves every OWN comparison on the employee link). **R2.3 merged first (DD-51):** deal's revision `d8a35c17e920` is written with `down_revision = "f3b8d1a65c02"`, the stages revision R2.3 creates, and **never** against `e94d7a2c5f18`, because `a1c9e2f7b3d4` is byte-pinned and a second revision on the old head would leave deal with two heads that only an edit to the pinned file could repair. R2.3 should also have been deployed and verified on its own; if not, one `make deploy` walks `alembic upgrade head` through both in order (safe, but it forfeits R2.3's own verification).
  R1.1 merged (docs). R2.4 is not required (if R2.4 has not merged, this release creates `services/customer/app/clients.py`; whichever merges first creates it).
- **Decisions** (the card that depends on an open row does not start before the owner answers it): D-7 (`owners` gains `membership_id`; the Team screen activates members; free-form rep creation retires after cutover), D-8 (a reviewed plan: `link` evidence for employee-valued rows, `email` evidence needs explicit acceptance, unmapped rows untouched and listed, never guess), D-10 (the owner's read-only census). The cards build the defaults. D-9 gates R2.7, not this release.
- **Operating model (DP-2.6-1).** ADR-0036 decision 1 says the **purge** tool has no `make` target and no `remote.sh` subcommand. The registry and spec choose the other shape for this tool: an owner-gated wrapper, the shape of `reconcile_permissions` (`infrastructure/edge/remote.sh:434-458`, registry §H preamble, spec §9.4, registry H1), because the tool must run three child processes in order in throwaway containers whose state directory belongs to the image's own user.
  The departure is deliberate and is recorded in `docs/adr/0038-crm-programme-decisions.md` and the RUNBOOK section (Task 2.6.11): the wrapper is owner-gated exactly like `make edge-reconcile` and an agent never runs it.
- **OWNER RUN items.** O-9: deploy four images, check three Alembic heads, publish the SPA from the merged checkout, run `census`, `plan`, and review the plan through `show`, `accept`, `reject` and `link`. `apply` belongs to R2.7's window.
- **Branch.** `feat/crm-r2-6-owner-expand`, cut from `main` after R2.3 is on `main`.

### Deploy order and verification

1. **Agent, before the PR is opened.** `make gate` locally with the output pasted into the PR; plus the two opt-in database runs, pass counts pasted into the PR (the gate skips them): the cross-schema end to end of Task 2.6.13 and the purge tool's own database test, because this release adds three append-only tables it must still reach:
   `OPSGRIDS_MAP_OWNERS_TEST_DATABASE_URL=<DSN as opsgrids_admin on a migrated throwaway database> uv run pytest tests/infra/test_map_crm_owners_e2e_db.py` and
   `OPSGRIDS_PURGE_ORGS_TEST_DATABASE_URL=<same DSN> uv run pytest tests/infra/test_purge_test_orgs_db.py` (`make migrate DATABASE_URL=<superuser DSN on the throwaway database>` first; `tests/infra/test_purge_test_orgs_db.py:1-20` says how to create it).
2. **OWNER RUN: review and squash-merge.**
3. **OWNER RUN: deploy.** `make deploy HOST=… CONFIRM=… REF=<sha>`. `libs/contracts` is excluded from the full-rebuild rule, so **four images rebuild and nothing else: `account`, `customer`, `deal`, `lead`.** Migrations run **before** `up` while the old code serves (`remote.sh` migrate step, `infrastructure/edge/remote.sh:243-301`): each of the three gains one additive revision (a nullable column, an empty table); old code ignores both, so the skew is safe.
4. **OWNER RUN: verify, read-only.**

   ```bash
   make edge-status HOST=… CONFIRM=…
   # on the box, from infrastructure/edge/ (the RUNBOOK pattern, RUNBOOK.md:744-752):
   for s in customer deal lead; do docker compose -f compose.prod.yml --env-file .env run --rm --no-deps -T $s alembic current; done
   ```

   Expect `b6d20f94e1a7 (head)`, `d8a35c17e920 (head)` and `a47e3b9d1c68 (head)`. `GET /api/v1/customers/owners` carries `membership_id: null` on every row. After the first candidates read, `make edge-logs HOST=… CONFIRM=… SERVICE=account TAIL=300` shows no 403 for `customer`.
5. **OWNER RUN: publish the SPA** from the checked-out merged `main` (the bundle is built from the local checkout, not from the deployed ref): `make edge-web HOST=… CONFIRM=… APP=crm`; prove the right tree was built by grepping the published bundle for `membership_id`
   (on the box: `grep -rl "membership_id" "$(sed -n 's/^EDGE_WEB_ROOT=//p' .env | head -1)/crm/current"`).
6. **OWNER RUN: census, then plan, then review (reads only; the plan is written to the box's state directory).**

   ```bash
   make edge-map-crm-owners HOST=… CONFIRM=… SUB=census                                  # D-10
   make edge-map-crm-owners HOST=… CONFIRM=… SUB=census ARGS=--aborted-conversions        # repeats R2.4's D-3 count
   make edge-map-crm-owners HOST=… CONFIRM=… SUB=plan                                     # writes plan.json, mode 600, owned by the image's user
   make edge-map-crm-owners HOST=… CONFIRM=… SUB=show ARGS="--org <uuid>"                 # ids and counts only
   make edge-map-crm-owners HOST=… CONFIRM=… SUB=show ARGS="--org <uuid> --print-emails"  # emails, to your own terminal only
   make edge-map-crm-owners HOST=… CONFIRM=… SUB=accept ARGS="--org <uuid> --ids <id,id>" # each email or manual row you accept
   make edge-map-crm-owners HOST=… CONFIRM=… SUB=link ARGS="--org <uuid> --owner-id <roster id> --membership-id <uuid>"   # a person the planner could not match
   make edge-map-crm-owners HOST=… CONFIRM=… SUB=plan                                     # a fresh plan carries each link as an unaccepted manual row
   ```

   The plan stays on the box until `forget-plan` (R2.7's step 7). **`apply` is not run in this release**; dual resolution means the owner *may* run it earlier, and the SPA of step 5 is what keeps that safe.
7. **Memory.** No container is added or resized: the totals stay at R2.4's (core 1772, `crm` 2068, ten profiles 3748, ten plus `admin` 3945); `account` stays `api_with_worker`; Postgres connections are unchanged.

### Rollback

Redeploy the previous ref (`make edge-rollback HOST=… CONFIRM=…`): the three revisions stay (expand-only, ignored by old code), and `remote.sh migrate` skips a service whose database is ahead of the image (`infrastructure/edge/lib/migration-revisions.sh`, pinned by `tests/infra/test_migration_revisions.py`). The SPA rolls back with
`make edge-web-rollback HOST=… CONFIRM=… APP=crm` (one symlink; **`APP=crm` is required**, the target defaults to the storefront's `buyer` bundle, `Makefile:625`). Nothing is rewritten by R2.6, so there is no data to restore. **If `apply` has been run**, code from before R2.6 knows only roster ids and cannot name a membership-valued row (the owner column would read "Unassigned"),
so run `revert --run-id` first (Task 2.6.8) and only then roll the code below R2.6. **Stop conditions:** any 5xx on the owners routes; `account` answering 403 to `customer`; an owner column rendering "Unassigned" for a record that has an owner; the candidates list failing for an organization with members.

**Files**

- Modify: `services/customer/app/models.py` (`Owner` `:65-92` gains the column and the partial index; add `OwnerRekeyJournal`)

**Interfaces**
- Produces, `down_revision = "e230c025337e"`, both revision lines carrying `# pragma: allowlist secret` as the neighbouring migrations do (`e230c025337e_case_insensitive_company_name.py:27-28`), opening with `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'`:

  ```sql
  ALTER TABLE customer.owners ADD COLUMN membership_id uuid;                 -- no foreign key: account is another schema
  CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_owners_org_membership ON customer.owners (organization_id, membership_id) WHERE membership_id IS NOT NULL;
  CREATE TABLE customer.owner_rekey_journal (
      id uuid NOT NULL, organization_id uuid NOT NULL, run_id uuid NOT NULL, table_name varchar(40) NOT NULL,
      row_id uuid NOT NULL, old_owner_id uuid NOT NULL, new_owner_id uuid NOT NULL, evidence varchar(12) NOT NULL,
      applied_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
      CONSTRAINT pk_owner_rekey_journal PRIMARY KEY (id),
      CONSTRAINT ck_owner_rekey_journal_evidence CHECK (evidence IN ('link', 'email', 'manual', 'revert')),
      CONSTRAINT ck_owner_rekey_journal_distinct CHECK (old_owner_id <> new_owner_id),
      CONSTRAINT ck_owner_rekey_journal_table CHECK (table_name IN ('owners', 'companies', 'contacts')));
  CREATE INDEX ix_customer_owner_rekey_journal_organization_id ON customer.owner_rekey_journal (organization_id);
  CREATE INDEX ix_owner_rekey_journal_org_run ON customer.owner_rekey_journal (organization_id, run_id);
  CREATE FUNCTION customer.forbid_journal_mutation() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN RAISE EXCEPTION 'owner_rekey_journal is append-only: % is not permitted', TG_OP; END $$;
  CREATE TRIGGER trg_owner_rekey_journal_append_only BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON customer.owner_rekey_journal FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION customer.forbid_journal_mutation();
  ALTER TABLE customer.owner_rekey_journal ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;  ALTER TABLE customer.owner_rekey_journal FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
  CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON customer.owner_rekey_journal FOR ALL TO opsgrids_customer USING (organization_id = customer.current_org()) WITH CHECK (organization_id = customer.current_org());
  ```

  No grant is written: `apply_schema_grants` re-grants DML on every table after each migration (`libs/platform-core/src/platform_core/db.py:56-87`), so the immutability is the trigger (it raises for every role, the shape of deal's `trg_activities_append_only`, `services/deal/migrations/versions/e94d7a2c5f18_enable_row_level_security.py:88-107`), not a revoke. Model side: `Owner.membership_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None]` plus the same partial index in `__table_args__` (so `make migration-check` sees no drift), and `OwnerRekeyJournal(Base)` with the columns above (not `TenantBase`: it has no `deleted_at`).
  **Guarded downgrade** (`OPSGRIDS_ALLOW_DESTRUCTIVE_DOWNGRADE`, the convention of `services/operations/migrations/versions/b7d41e92c05a_lots_rolls_genealogy.py:496-519`): refuses while the journal holds any row or any `owners.membership_id` is set, unless the override is set; empty, it drops the trigger, function, policy, journal, index and column.
- Rules that hold for the whole release: the journal carries ids only, no PII; every query the tool and the activation path run on these tables carries `organization_id = :org` as well as the bound tenant GUC; `owners.id` is never rekeyed and `owners.membership_id` is never edited once set (route-level: `PATCH` forbids it).

### Task 2.6.4: Account: the bulk membership read (registry C57)

**Files**
- Modify: `services/account/app/api/internal.py` (beside `membership_lookup`, `:304-346`; the router is `include_in_schema=False`, `:69-76`; `SessionDep` is the BYPASSRLS SELECT-only directory session, `:82`)
- Modify: `services/account/app/selectors.py` (add `list_directory_members`; the point read is `get_member`, `:171-184`)
- Modify: `services/account/app/schemas.py` (add `DirectoryMemberOut`, `DirectoryMembersOut`)
- Create: `services/account/tests/test_internal_memberships.py`

**Interfaces**
- Produces `GET /internal/v1/organizations/{organization_id}/memberships`.
  Auth: `require_service_token` (router-level), caller allow-list **`customer` only in this release** (`_require_caller(request, "customer")`; registry `C57` adds each caller with its first use, least privilege: `customer` from R2.6, `deal` and `lead` from R3.8's second deploy), the token's `org` claim must equal the path organization (`_require_org_claim`; 403 otherwise; the shape of `services/deal/app/api/internal.py:64-80`; the existing route checks its caller inline, `:333-336`).
  Query: `after_id: uuid | None` (keyset), `limit: int` 1 to 500 default 200, `ids: str | None` (a comma list of at most 100 uuids; when present the result is exactly those that belong to the organization).
  Response `DirectoryMembersOut {items: [{membership_id, full_name, email, status, is_owner, employee_id, manager_membership_id}], next_after_id: uuid | None}` ordered by `Membership.id`; `full_name = coalesce(nullif(display_name, ''), users.full_name)`; **every status is returned, `removed` included**, so a plan can say why a roster email matches nobody. `next_after_id = rows[-1].id` when the page is full, else `null`.
  Errors: 401, 403 (wrong caller; wrong or missing organization claim), 422 (malformed uuid, `limit` outside 1 to 500, more than 100 ids). Fields never returned: credentials, sessions, MFA state, the user's phone, roles.
  The query carries an explicit `Membership.organization_id == :organization_id` predicate on top of the directory session (a BYPASSRLS reader has no RLS to lean on), joins `users`, and never writes.

- `POST /customers/owners` with a `membership_id`: **claim, call, record, and the account call is never inside a transaction**. Both new/changed routes take `RawSessionDep = Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(get_session)]` and open their own `async with session.begin():` blocks, binding the tenant first with `set_tenant` as the first statement of each
  (the precedent is `services/lead/app/api/routes.py:62,239-270` and `services/lead/app/services.py:94-102`; `get_tenant_session` holds one transaction open for the whole handler, which `tests/infra/test_io_outside_transaction.py` flags for any network call).
  (1) Claim, a read-only transaction: 409 `already_activated` if a roster row already holds this `membership_id`. (2) Call, no transaction: `fetch_member`; unreachable, timeout or 5xx is 503 `upstream-unavailable` and nothing is written; an id unknown to this organization is 404 `membership_not_found`; a status other than `active` is 422 `membership_not_active`.
  (3) Record, a transaction: re-check `already_activated` under the partial unique index (a race answers 409); refuse with 409 `owner_email_exists`, naming that roster row's id in the message, when any roster row of the organization already has the member's email compared case-insensitively (the owner links that row with the mapping tool instead of creating a second person); insert the row with `membership_id`, `full_name` (cut to 160), `email`, `role` (the body's, default empty), `is_active = true`;
  audit `owner.created` with `after = {membership_id, activated: true}` (ids only, no name or email); the existing behaviour of `create_owner` (reference data, no domain event) is unchanged. `services.create_owner(..., membership_id: uuid.UUID | None = None)` gains the keyword for seeds and tests (Task 2.7.7).
- **Error encoding.** Each named code (`already_activated`, `owner_email_exists`, `membership_not_found`, `membership_not_active`, and R2.7's `membership_required`) is an `errors[]` entry `{field, code, message}` on the RFC 7807 body of the matching `platform_core.errors` class (`ConflictProblem` 409, `NotFoundProblem` 404, `ValidationProblem` 422), the shape Task 2.5.4 fixes for the stage errors; the 503 is `UpstreamUnavailableProblem` (`problem_type = "upstream-unavailable"`, `libs/platform-core/src/platform_core/errors.py:126-129`). A client reads `code`, not the message.
- `GET /customers/owners/candidates` (C27): `crm.book.owner.write`, `minimum=Scope.ORG`, `dependencies=[Entitled]`; response `{items: [{membership_id, full_name, email, status, is_owner, manager_membership_id}]}`: the **active** members with no roster row. The account call runs first (paged internally up to 5,000 members, 503 rather than a partial list), then one read-only transaction reads the roster's membership ids.

### Task 2.6.6: Customer: dual resolution at the server-side roster lookups (DD-28)

**Files**
- Modify: `services/customer/app/selectors.py` (`get_owner` `:44-52`, `get_owner_for_update` `:64-86`, `active_owner_ids` `:89-102`, `count_open_records_for_owner` `:105-134`)
- Modify: `services/customer/app/services.py` (`_assert_owner_assignable` `:187-206`; `deactivate_owner`'s call `:314-316`; `invalid_owner_ids` `:1085-1093`, which backs `owners:validate`)
- Create: `services/customer/tests/test_owner_dual_resolution.py`
- The 360's owner name (`services/customer/app/api/c1_customer360.py:63`, `OwnerRef` at `c1_360.py:318`) and `POST /internal/v1/organizations/{id}/owners:validate` (`api/internal.py:351-380`) follow through `get_owner` and `invalid_owner_ids` with **no route edit**; their request and response shapes are unchanged.

**Interfaces**
- One shared rule for a reference `r` (the org's rows, `deleted_at IS NULL`): it resolves to the roster row `ORDER BY (membership_id = r) DESC LIMIT 1` over `membership_id = r OR id = r`, so a membership id wins if both could match (they cannot in practice, both are random uuids; the order only makes the rule deterministic).
  Sites 1 to 5 of the spec's table are server-side: `get_owner`, `get_owner_for_update` (row-locked, `populate_existing=True`), `active_owner_ids` (returns the set of **references as posted** that resolve to an active row: for each matching row both its `id` and its `membership_id` are in the set), `count_open_records_for_owner(session, org_id, owner_id, membership_id=None)` (counts live companies and contacts whose `owner_id` is the row's `id` **or** its `membership_id`), and the 360's owner name.
  Sites 6 and 7 are the SPA (Task 2.6.10). Writes store the reference **as posted**: no server-side canonicalisation (the SPA posts the membership id for any owner that has one, and `verify` lists strays).
- `_assert_owner_assignable` keeps its OWN rule on `ctx.subject_ref` unchanged (R2.7 changes it to `own_ref`); only the resolution becomes dual. `deactivate_owner` passes the row's `membership_id` so a rep whose records were rewritten cannot be deactivated while they still own live ones.

- `test_get_owner_resolves_a_legacy_and_a_membership_reference` — act: `get_owner(session, org, L)` and `(…, M)`; assert both return `R`.
- `test_get_owner_for_update_resolves_both_and_locks_the_row` — assert both resolve and that a second session's lookup of the same row blocks under `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '300ms'` until the first commits.
- `test_active_owner_ids_returns_the_references_as_posted_that_resolve` — post `L`, `M` and an unknown `X`; assert the result holds `L` and `M` and not `X`; a deactivated `R` yields the empty set.
- `test_count_open_records_counts_both_kinds_of_id` — arrange: a company owned by `L` and a contact owned by `M`; assert the count is 2.
- `test_assert_owner_assignable_accepts_either_reference` (service level) — assert no error for `L` or `M`, and that an OWN caller still may assign only to their own `subject_ref` (the rule is untouched).
- `test_owners_validate_accepts_either_kind_of_id` — through the route with a `lead`-caller token: `invalid_owner_ids` is empty for `L` and for `M` and names `X`; its three negative tests (no token 401, wrong caller 403, wrong organization claim 403) stay green unedited.
- `test_the_360_owner_name_resolves_by_either_reference` — arrange: a contact whose `owner_id` is `M`; act: `GET /customers/{contact_id}/360` with the fake upstreams of `services/customer/tests/test_c1_customer360.py`; assert `body["customer"]["owner"]["name"]` is `R`'s name (`:131` shows the shape).
